name: iNaturalist Ecology Subset
description: Curated subset of iNaturalist research-grade observations for ecological pattern discovery

patterns.description: Observations are concentrated in North America and Europe due to iNaturalist user demographics
The dataset spans multiple taxonomic classes (Insecta, Mammalia, Aves, Magnoliopsida, Agaricomycetes) reflecting broad ecological diversity
Common Sunflower observations peak in summer-autumn months (July-October) during flowering season
Fly Agaric observations are strongly concentrated in autumn (September-November) corresponding to fruiting season
Monarch Butterfly observations show northward movement through spring-summer (latitude increases with month March-August in Northern Hemisphere), reflecting migration
Barn Swallow observations shift northward through spring, reflecting their well-known migration timing
Red Fox observations span a wider latitude range (25-70N) than most other species, reflecting their adaptability across biomes from desert to arctic
American Robin observations shift northward through spring-summer, reflecting their partial migration pattern
Plant species (Plantae) observations are more concentrated in spring-summer than animal species, reflecting flowering and leaf-out phenology
Dandelion observations peak earlier in the year (March-May) than most other species, as one of the first wildflowers to bloom
Red Deer observations are concentrated at higher latitudes (45-60N), reflecting their temperate/boreal habitat preference
Species with strong seasonal patterns show inverted observation peaks between Northern and Southern hemispheres (e.g., autumn mushrooms appear in March-May in Southern Hemisphere)
